newsitem.title: USA: Cellular group says U.S. government blocks antenna sites.
newsitem.headline: Cellular group says U.S. government blocks antenna sites.

text.p: The cellular phone industry complained to President Clinton Monday that the National Park Service and other U.S. agencies are thwarting industry efforts to install cellular antennas on or near federal lands.

The Cellular Telecommunications Industry Association said the agencies -- the Bureau of Land Management, the U.S. Forest Service, the Department of Defence and the General Services Administration -- are violating the new communications law and a presidential order on antenna-siting procedures.

"The wireless telecommunications industry continues to experience significant antenna siting resistance from far too many federal agencies in defiance of your order and the law," CTIA President Thomas Wheeler said in a letter to Clinton.

"The federal government, which once enabled the rights-of-way for railroads and highways, is now actively inhibiting a national wireless communications network for the 21st Century," added Wheeler, who sought presidential help.

Wheeler noted -- among other examples -- that the White House Office of Communications is unable to offer "quality" wireless service at the Camp David presidential retreat in rural Maryland because of the park service's refusal to allow antennas to be situated in the surrounding area.

He also complained that the park service -- in addition to denying siting requests on its own land -- "formally solicited 29 local and county governments to 'discourage the siting of towers'" to accommodate drivers on the Blue Ridge Parkway.
